title: CBE; Companion IEE
brief_context: The foundation was dedicated to her memory.
brief_extract:
THE ELECTRIC LIVING
FOUNDATION

The Foundation, dedicated at the EAW's Diamond Jubilee Service of Thanksgiving on 13 November 1984 to the memory of Mary George, CBE, Companion IEE, starts its work on 1 April 1985 under the EAW 'flag'. Will it prove the key to the Association's future?

title: Dame
brief_context: Her thoughts provided the inspiration for the foundation.
brief_extract: Will it prove the key to the Association's future? It was the thoughts of Dame Caroline Haslett, founding Director of the EAW, that provided the inspiration for the EAW's new specialist unit, the Electric Living Foundation. Reporting on the first World Power Conference (1924) in the Woman Engineer, Dame Caroline wrote of the wide gap that then existed between the suppliers of electricity, the makers of electrical appliances and the women who were their potential customers at that time.

brief_context: Quoted regarding not planning the future by the past.
article_title: FOCUS : 2000 Now it's time to ACCENTUATE THE POSITIVE!
brief_extract: All these questions demand answers. As Edmund Burke said, 'You cannot plan the future by the past.' The NEC is alert to the perils of looking backwards. Nostalgia can be seductive, but it is also very dangerous.

title: Dame
brief_context: Founding Director of EAW whose philosophy is mentioned.
article_title: FOCUS : 2000 Now it's time to ACCENTUATE THE POSITIVE!
brief_extract: It is a year for enthusiasm and tenacity, unfettered by narrow-mindedness and the limitations of tunnel vision. 'Get things done.' That was one of the favourite axioms of Dame Caroline Haslett, our Founding Director. For every reader who believes that the EAW's work in this country is too valuable to be lost to future users, there is a message that stems from Dame Caroline's own philosophy of action rather than words.

title: MIHEc
brief_context: Managing Executive of the Electric Living Foundation.
brief_extract: It should be remembered, though, that all these undertakings are part of a developing, ongoing programme, and the first year of the Foundation's work will be devoted to the early stages of that development. Initially there will be four staff (three fully-qualified home economists and a senior secretary) working under Norah Riddington MIHEc, the Foundation's Managing Executive. She will report through the EAW's Director, Ann McMullan MBE, to the Association's National Executive.

A stimulating programme made it all worth while for the 22 Associate Members who travelled from as far afield as the Midlands, East Anglia and the South West Coast to attend this special day. Mr Charles George, a member of the Guildford branch and a one time Associate Member, opened the morning session with a fascinating talk which he called An Electrifying Century. Since his retirement as Marketing Adviser to The Electricity Council Mr George has made a detailed study of the development of the usage of electricity in the home, basing his research on archives held in Brighton as well as on personal experiences of his early years working there.

The electrical history of Gibraltar began in 1895 when Sir William Preece was briefed to advise on the introduction of electric light in Gibraltar and Malta. Interestingly, Ewbank Preece still continue to act as consultants to the Electricity Department of the Gibraltar government.

title: General
brief_context: Directed operations during the Great Siege of 1779-1783.
article_title: EAW CONNECTS WITH POWER ON THE 'ROCK'
brief_extract: By 1897 the first steam generating facilities were in operation, and Gibraltar's streets were lit by electricity, only 15 years after those of Godalming. The first generating station was situated in the Kings Bastion, a key position from which General Eliott, the British Governor, had directed operations during the Great Siege of 1779-1783. Even a hundred years later it was still considered desirable as a site well-protected from gun-fire.

OBITUARY

LADY
HORNSBY-SMITH

Baroness Hornsby-Smith who died in July
1985 at the age of 71 was appointed
President of the EAW in 1975 after a
distinguished career in politics and service
to the community. Part of her early working life was spent
in the electrical industry.

title: Prime Minister
brief_context: Mentioned regarding constituency seat merger and peerage
brief_extract:
She held office as Parliamentary
Secretary to the Ministry of Health (being
at that time the youngest woman to have
held office in any government), Under
Secretary of State to the Home Office and
later of Pensions and National Insurance. The merger of her Chislehurst
constituency with that of next door Bexley,
Prime Minister Heath's seat, meant she was
elbowed out in the 1974 election and never
returned to the House of Commons. She
was however made a life peeress in Heath's
retirement honours list.

title: Miss
brief_context: Interviewed Baroness Hornsby-Smith in 1975
brief_extract:
She was Vice-President of the
Commercial Travellers' Benevolent
Institution; Vice-President of the
Association of Metropolitan Authorities; a
Freeman of the City of London; and a
Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts. Interviewed for the Autumn 1975 issue of
Electrical Age by Miss Mary George, the
Baroness agreed that electricity is the safest
fuel for disabled people, provided, as she
added, that the equipment is of the right
kind, properly installed and maintained. She also stressed the importance of the
educational work done by the EAW in
promoting its courses of instruction in
schools and technical colleges.
